title: A Budgeted Robust Cohort-Transition Model for Enrollment Capacity Planning Under Demographic Decline
content: Low fertility reaches university admissions only after a long delay and then propagates through several years of enrollment stock. This timing creates a capacity-planning problem that annual enrollment forecasts do not resolve. We formulate an integrated cohort-transition model that converts observed births into a recruitment-weighted admission index, propagates intake through a four-grade stock, and chooses adult, enterprise-training, and international full-time-equivalent capacity in a linear program. A Bertsimas–Sim budget limits how many active admission cohorts can simultaneously attain their adverse bounds. In a publicly reproducible case calibrated to a 21,136-student vocational university, nominal traditional enrollment falls to 12,125 in 2043. At a baseline uncertainty budget of two, its robust lower path is 11,505 and an 85% resilience floor requires 6461 nontraditional FTEs at the peak; the corresponding peaks are 5841 with no budgeted protection and 7024 under the full four-cohort budget. A reported-intake one-step accounting check has 3.7% absolute percentage error. Kernel, initialization, mechanism-ablation, global-sensitivity, and operational-sensitivity experiments identify the resilience floor, cohort elasticity, uncertainty budget, and attraction loss as the main planning drivers. The framework supplies a transparent bridge from demographic exposure to ramp-constrained capacity decisions without presenting scenario parameters as statistical forecasts.
